Passive of Modal Verbs Must and Should
The passive voice is used when we want to emphasize the action (the verb) and the object of a sentence rather than the subject.

We can use should in passive voice when we want to give a suggestion or piece of advice focusing on the action instead of the performer of it. Use must when talking about obligations.

Use the following structure to make affirmative statements with these modals:

Here is the grammar structure we use:

Subject + must be/should be + past participle verb form + complement

Examples:
Big data must be studied thoroughly.
Information systems management should be used properly in companies.
This article should be studied by everybody, including system engineers.
Intelligence systems should be able to automate data collection.

Sandy: Everything is changing constantly, especially in our field!
Pearl: Information systems management must change. It is required for companies if they want to survive. I read an article about this.
Sandy: What was the article about?
Pearl: It's an article about trends that will impact information systems. This article should be studied by everybody, including system engineers.
Sandy: What trends do they mention in this article?
Pearl: They mention three trends. The first trend is data collection automation. Intelligence systems should be able to automate data collection. Also, intelligence systems must be implemented by companies to collect information quicker to identify and respond to emerging market opportunities. Information analysis automation is the second trend. Companies will need to implement automated data collection; big data must be considered very influential in market intelligence activities. The last trend is the cross function integration. Information collection and information analysis programs should be integrated with other organizational functions in the future.

Sandy: Will these trends change information systems management?
Pearl: Indeed, Sandy. The needs of users of information management system change quickly. Companies will have to adapt to more sophisticated systems that combine all the data collected within their organization. Data collection and information analysis must be used to interpret and study, both negative and positive market signals.

Sandy: So, it will help make better decisions in our company.
Pearl: Exactly. We need to use technology to our advantage. There are statistical and modeling tools that we can use taking into consideration the company's specific circumstances and goals to grow. These trends also tell us that the information management systems will handle more data and at a faster speed. So, if we don't do this, our competition will, and we will be left behind.

There are some steps to follow when you want to write an outline for a text about future trends in information system management.

Follow the next steps to write an outline.

Instructions:

  • Look for further information on future trends in information system management.
  • Write a title depending on the intention of your text: either to persuade or inform your reader, or to make a reflection on the trends in information system management.
  • Choose the way you're going to present your information: topic outline (key words) or sentence outline.
  • Make a list of the ideas you're going to include to develop the topics in your text (3 main trends in information systems management).
  • Below each idea, include main subtopics using Roman numerals.
  • Add extra ideas per subtopic. At least two using supporting sentences. Expand them if necessary.
  • Write a concluding sentence for your text. Restate the main point of your text (persuade, inform, reflect).

    When you have typed in ALL your answers, click the Go to Writing Task button.

It's time to review your outline.  </br></br>

When you are writing your outline, remember to include: </br></br>

•  A title that includes the intention of your text.</br>
•  Ideas that develop your main idea.</br>
•  Subtopics that develop each idea.</br>
•  Supporting sentences that develop each subtopic.</br>
•  A concluding sentence</br></br></br>
